body:
The driver's state *is* the files under `results/issue_<id>/` — nothing is hidden in a database.
So a bundle that reaches a halted state and is never committed is state that exists on one
machine only: invisible to an Act review across frozen cycles, to a second operator, and to any
later reader asking why a contribution looks the way it does. Recording is currently a manual
`git add results/issue_N && git commit` that is easy to forget, and the forgetting is silent.

Observed in the wyrd instance: four bundles sat uncommitted across five days — 507, 509 and 510
(COMPLETE, each already shipped as its own upstream PR) and 626 (DISCONTINUED). The 626 case is
the sharp one: its §9 records the decision that produced an upstream PR, so while the bundle was
uncommitted, the *provenance for an open PR* existed nowhere but one working tree.

## Proposal

A `pdca record [<ids>…]` verb (no ids ⇒ every unrecorded bundle) that classifies with
`state.state`, stages the halted ones, commits with a conventional subject, and — when the
instance opts in — branches, pushes and opens one PR for the batch. Deterministic git/gh
subprocesses, no model in the loop, same shape as `publish.py`'s git steps.

```toml
[records]
mode    = "pr"                                # off (default) | commit | pr
branch  = "docs/{issue}-record-{ids}"
subject = "docs(results): record bundles {ids}"
issue   = "ask"                               # ask | <N> (a standing records issue)
```

`mode = "off"` by default keeps every existing instance unaffected, including instances that do
not version `results/` at all or do not use GitHub. This is the same engine/instance split
`[publisher].fix_branch_pattern` and `[publisher.checkouts]` already use: mechanism in the
engine, project specifics in `pdca.toml`.

## Three design points, each learned from getting them wrong by hand

**1. The trigger is "terminal", not "published".** The obvious hook is "after `publish` succeeds",
but publish only covers `COMPLETE`. A `DISCONTINUED` bundle never publishes and still needs
recording — 626 above — as does `RESOLVED`. The condition should be `state.state(d) in HALTED`
minus `UNPLANNED`/`AWAITING_SIGNOFF` (which are halted-for-a-human, not finished), i.e. COMPLETE,
DISCONTINUED, RESOLVED. Publish is then one path in, not the definition.

**2. It must run *after* publish, never inside it.** `publish()` writes `publish.json` (branch,
`pr_url`, base, repo) into the bundle as its closing act, so a hook firing mid-publish records a
bundle that is about to change and pins the wrong bytes. If publish triggers it, the call belongs
after that write.

**3. Batch by default; one PR per bundle is noise.** The wyrd instance's own history records 4–6
bundles per PR (`docs(results): record bundles 503/504/505/506`, `…507/509/510 and the
discontinued 626`). Per-bundle PRs also multiply against an instance rule of one issue per PR.

**Bundles in motion must be excluded, and that is the whole safety property.** `issue_508` in the
wyrd instance is UNPLANNED (its brief archived, blocked on another cycle's design document);
sweeping it in would commit a bundle that is still being rewritten. `state.state` already answers
this exactly — which is the main argument for the engine owning it rather than a script
reimplementing the classification.

## Why the engine rather than an instance script

- The classification is `state.state`; a script has to reimplement or shell out to it, and a
  reimplementation drifts (the RESOLVED-guard defect in the wyrd instance was exactly two
  enumerations of "what a cycle writes" drifting apart).
- `flow --no-publish`, `publish`, and the Act pass can all call one entry point, so a cycle that
  ends in any halted state records itself the same way.
- Every instance that versions `results/` needs it; the parts that differ (branch pattern, PR or
  no PR, how an issue is linked) are exactly the parts config already expresses.

The wyrd instance can carry an interim `scripts/record-bundles` on the `scripts/review-branch`
precedent, retired when this lands.
title: pdca record: commit terminal result bundles to the instance repo (and open one PR for the batch)
